about.title: Highland Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Highland's mix of retail corridors, warehouses, and roadwork along SR-210 means workplace injuries here range from warehouse falls to job-site vehicle collisions on Baseline Street or 9th Street. In California, workers' compensation is generally the exclusive remedy against your employer, no matter who was at fault — but that doesn't always cover the full picture. If a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate third-party claim worth pursuing. Highland's roughly 55,000 residents work across construction, distribution, and service industries where these overlapping claims come up often. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect injured workers with an independent attorney who can sort out what applies to your situation, review your paperwork, and explain your options without cost to start.

items.title: Third-Party Claims Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually your exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party like a subcontractor or equipment maker can still be held separately liable. An attorney can help determine if that applies to your Highland workplace injury.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from retaliating against workers who report injuries. If you reported within 30 days and faced pushback, an attorney in our network can advise you on your rights.

items.title: Awareness of Filing Deadlines
items.desc: While workers' comp has its own reporting rules, any third-party injury claim in California generally must be filed within two years. Missing that window can close off compensation you're otherwise owed.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near SR-210 in Highland — do I file workers' comp or a lawsuit?
items.answer: Likely both should be considered. Workers' comp usually applies first since it's the exclusive remedy against your employer, but if another party — like a contractor or driver — contributed to the crash, you may also have a separate claim. An independent attorney can review the details and tell you what fits your situation.

items.question: What if my employer told me not to report the injury?
items.answer: California law requires you to report a workplace injury within 30 days, and it's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for doing so. If you've faced pressure not to report, that's worth discussing with an attorney promptly.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, connecting with an attorney through LawProactive is free. Attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
